torn.story: It touched down south-west of Saragosa at about 8:15 PM as a narrow F2, curling once as it formed, and tracked north-east parallel to Highway 17. At the village it grew to more than half a mile across and F4, and most of the village's homes were destroyed. In the community hall a pre-school graduation was under way; the hall collapsed and 22 people inside were killed. The warning had gone out in English to a village that mostly spoke Spanish. North of the village it turned north, snapping eight power poles 300 feet apart and throwing cars and trucks 300 to 500 feet, then hooked west and died out. 30 dead, 121 injured.

story: Saragosa was a small, largely Spanish-speaking farming community in the Toyah Valley of west Texas. On the evening of 22 May 1987, many of its families were gathered in the parish hall of Our Lady of Guadalupe church for a Head Start graduation.
The tornado that crossed the town was rated F4. It destroyed the hall along with most of the town, and twenty-two of the people inside were killed; thirty died in all.

A tornado warning had been issued, but it reached Saragosa in English, on English-language media, to a community that largely did not use them. The disaster became a turning point in how warnings are delivered to people who do not speak the language they are written in.
